EVENT_NARRATIVE: Minor damage to homes resulted when a dust devil moved through this community.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A possible dust devil descended the foothills just west of Carson City. Flying debris generated by the dust devil damaged 12 automobiles in the DMV parking lot.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong surface heating due to sunshine combined with localized winds to produce a dust devil.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Patio furniture was damaged and a woman was injured in Valley Lee due to a dust devil.

The dust devil ripped the aluminum roof off a porch and scattered pieces of it down the block.  Metal sheeting was also blown into powerlines, knocking out power to around 700 people. EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected dust devil damaged several mobile homes in the Desert Inn Estates Mobile Home Park.  Debris from one of the homes also damaged a car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms occurred across the eastern Sierra and far western Nevada.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil was observed in a field west of Pyramid Highway at Calle de la Plata north of Reno.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong heating helped fuel a dust devil in Henderson.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil damaged approximately 12 homes in the Mountain View Mobile Home Park.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: An aluminum overhang was torn off of a mobile home in Ruskin. There was flat cumulus and interviews with two eye witnesses both said there was rotation at the ground. It was determined this was a dust devil.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A back door cold front early on the 17th provided a fresh supply of low level moisture over eastern New Mexico. Southeast low level winds and moderate northwest flow aloft allowed for strong shear, producing long lived and severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The strong dust devil produced some damage, including ripping the metal siding off a hay barn, damaging a coral and knocking over a 5th wheel trailer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil produced strong winds just west of Fruita.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil traveled directly into an anemometer which measured a peak wind gust of 66 mph.  Unsecured items were blown over and tossed about.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: One mobile home was moved off its foundation, and the roof was blown off another.  Based on the description of the event, a dust devil is suspected.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong sunshine and temperatures 10-15 degrees above average helped spin up a dust devil which caused damage in Boulder City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong dust devil moved through the Gingerwood Mobile Home Park on the edge of Boulder City, damaging several mobile homes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil which was particularly unusual because it occurred on a cool morning damaged a plane at the Mesquite Municipal Airport.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil flipped over a Cessna on the tarmac at Mesquite Municipal Airport.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sunshine and light winds lead to the development of a relatively strong dust devil in northern Lincoln County near Gilbert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil formed during the afternoon on a sunny, mild day, and moved through the backyard of a family home. The dust devil picked up a trampoline, threw it 10 feet in the air, and smashed it into the side of a garage. The whirlwind continued through the yard and picked up burning corn stalks and paper from a fire barrel, swirling the debris around. The dust devil crossed a nearby road into a field and dissipated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil moved along a dock on the southern branch of the Oconto River and did damage to the dock and a nearby pontoon boat.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At around 3 pm CDT, a dust devil formed near the Machickanee Flowage on the southern branch of the Oconto River near Stiles.  The whirlwind moved onto the water for a brief time, lifting the back of a pontoon boat and sucking the life jackets into the air.  It then lifted several sections of the end of the dock 40 feet into the air, spinning the debris around, finally depositing everything into the water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil momentarily lifted several children off the ground at Makaha Elementary School in West Oahu, causing a few minor injuries.  There were no reports of property damage.  Wind gusts with the dust devil were estimated near 60 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Under a strong area of high pressure. There was enough instability near the surface with daytime heating to produce a strong dust devil in Franklin Parish in Winnsboro. It blew the metal roof and insulation off of a small storage building and damaged some nearby trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong dust devil blew the metal roof and insulation off of a small storage building. Some nearby trees were bent to near the point of snapping. It was reported by the Franklin Sun newspaper.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil occurred at the Rockhound Show at the fairgrounds just south of Madras. Several canopies from vendors were destroyed with tarps in the trees.  Although nobody was injured, a tray of rocks tossed and hit one man.  A 25-lb lead ball that was used as a paperweight was found on top of an awning of a motorhome.  A vehicle was forced into another vehicle.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil occurred during a very hot and unstable afternoon with light winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A very well-defined dust devil was observed. The dust devil was roughly ten feet wide at the base and about 60 feet tall. It travelled around 80 feet before dissipating.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dust devils formed over drought-parched fields on a very warm and sunny afternoon with light winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An off-duty meteorologist observed three or four dust devils on U.S. Highway 60 between Wyatt and Charleston in Mississippi County. The funnels were visible up to 20 feet above ground level.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The dust devils formed over drought-parched fields on a very warm and sunny afternoon with light winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained spotter photographed a dust devil passing through farm fields in the Fort Branch area. The dust devil was on the ground for over a mile and grew to 40 feet in diameter at times. Multiple vortices were seen dancing around the main vortex. This was the only confirmed dust devil. However, conditions were ripe for dust devils each afternoon from the 6th to the 8th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A well-defined dust devil moved through parts of leeward Oahu, between Kapolei and Kunia, and received a great deal of publicity; but it did not lead to any serious property damage or injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A gustnado underneath very high cloud bases and along the leading edge of strong outflow from a high based shower lasted at least 5 minutes.  There were a few reports that this was a tornado but close examination revealed a gustnado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A gustnado or dust devil underneath very high cloud bases and along the leading edge of outflow from a high based shower lasted at least 5 minutes. There were a few reports that this was a tornado but close examination revealed a gustnado or dust devil.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil struck a mobile home in Mohave Valley, causing minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil damaged an awning on a mobile home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large dust devil moved through the community of Desert Hills in north Phoenix and caused damage to one of the homes in the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At 2 pm on May 13, a huge dust devil passed over a home in Desert Hills, located between Anthem and Cave Creek in north Phoenix. The dust devil tore a number of shingles off of the roof, and flipped a swingset into their barn. According to the homeowner, the dust devil sounded like a freight train running through the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil resulted in a brief severe wind gust of 59 mph that was recorded by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Abernathy (Hale County) just before 13:25 CST on the 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil was thought to be the cause of minor damage at a resident's house just southwest of Clayton, Washington.  The region was located under a cool upper-level trough with fair cumulus at the time of the event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A resident located southwest of Clayton, WA sustained minor damage to her trailer when a strong dust devil moved across her property.  The dust devil ripped siding off of both sides of her trailer.  The siding landed in her neighbor���s horse pasture. It also picked up her trampoline and threw it several feet.  There were no injuries.  Damage costs were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure and record high temperatures created a very unstable and dry environment resulting in several dust devils.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong daytime heating resulting in record high temperatures and dry conditions created a ripe environment for dust devils. One dust devil formed near Speedway Blvd. and N. 11th Ave. where an annual Children's Festival was in progress. The dust devil quickly moved across the yard lifting a jumping castle several feet into the air with two children inside. The jumping castle then traveled several feet before getting caught in telephone wires and landing in the median of Speedway Blvd. A 9-year-old girl was serious injured in the accident, suffering a broken shoulder, leg, and several fractures to her face. A 10-year-old boy also sustained injuries to the back of his head.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong daytime heating and an unstable atmosphere created prime conditions for dust devils.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong daytime heating and unstable conditions caused several dust devils to form across the region. One dust devil formed at Hoffman Park located at the 4800 block of South Cecilia St. in Tucson. Parents were able to pull their children out of a jumping castle just before the stakes were pulled out of the ground as the jumping castle was lifted several feet into the funnel and tossed into a light pole. The dust devil also picked up several other pieces of debris before dissipating over the concrete street. Six children were injured by flying debris. Five were evaluated at the scene, while one 16-year-old boy was transported to a hospital with minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure brought light gradient winds with good diurnal heating conditions producing steep low level lapse rates. A local temperature variation between land and nearby Lake Monona created a localized shear zone that led to the formation of a dust devil near Monona...southeast of the city of Madison. The dust devil developed over the Yahara River, traveled south, and came ashore where it picked up a plastic storage shed located near the Four Lake Yacht Club and blew off the roof of the shed.

The dust devil formed in the Central Heights area, a subdivision between Globe and Miami. According to an article in the Copper Country News, the dust devil collapsed an above ground pool. The water from the pool then brought down a concrete and rock retaining wall. The wall collapsed on top of a car, crushing and severely damaging the car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clear skies, light winds and intense midday solar heating allowed a dust devil to develop near Hosmer Lake, west of Bend.

Four or five small vendor tents were picked up and tossed into the air. There were a few minor injuries. One person had a bruise on the arm and another was hit in the head with a tent pole.

Four or five small vendor tents were picked up and tossed into the air causing a few minor injuries. One person had a bruise on the arm and another was hit in the head with a tent pole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil in North Las Vegas damaged a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil hit a home near Grand Teton and Aliante Parkway, taking 20 to 30 tiles off the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot temperatures helped fuel a dust devil in the Las Vegas Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil destroyed a fireworks stand in front of the Walmart in the 4500 block of West Charleston Blvd. in Las Vegas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The heat and drought led to many well-developed dust devils in July. One of these damaged a business on the 31st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil damaged a business in the Amboy section of North Little Rock. A metal awning was peeled off and part of the metal roof of a building was peeled back.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil developed in a field in Weakley County and caused some damage near Dresden.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil began in a bean field and moved northwest to southeast. It tore apart a fiberglass well housing. The dust devil picked up a metal burn barrel and spread the contents several hundred feet into the air. Part of a roof was also torn off. Some of the debris damaged a brand new car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unusually hot weather that began in late June continued into the first part of July, thanks to a large area of high pressure aloft. Many high temperatures of 100 degrees or higher were recorded, and a number of daily high temperature records were broken. Although enough moisture returned such that very isolated showers and thunderstorms occurred each day, the rain did little to help the drought. Early in the month, about a third of Arkansas was affected by extreme drought, with severe drought existing in almost all other parts of the state. Pastures dried up, causing many cattle growers to send their livestock to market. Some stock ponds dried up, as well. Some water utilities instituted mandatory water restrictions. The hot, dry weather contributed to the spread of wildfires. At the beginning of the month, the Arkansas Forestry Commission rated fire danger statewide as Extreme, a category which is used very rarely. County judges instituted burn bans for virtually every county in Arkansas. Sales of fireworks for the 4th of July were greatly affected, with some fireworks stands closing before the holiday. Some municipal fireworks shows were cancelled as a result of the dry weather. Dozens of fires broke out each day, but only a relatively small number of these exceeded 100 acres. On the 3rd, Arkansas Governor Mike Beebe authorized the National Guard to use Black Hawk helicopters to assist firefighters by dropping water on the larger fires using 660 gallon Bambi Buckets. On the 4th alone, the Arkansas Forestry Commission fought 43 wildfires which burned 1803 acres. During the first half of the month, many rivers in the state fell to unusually low levels. Twenty stations recorded levels that were in their top ten lowest water levels since the last big agricultural drought in 2000. The U.S. Secretary of Agriculture designated almost all of Arkansas as being in a drought disaster. Tropical moisture began returning to Arkansas about the 6th of July. This brought higher humidities, somewhat of an increase in afternoon showers and thunderstorms, and caused the number of wildfires each day to diminish. On the 17th, the Arkansas Forestry Commission dropped the wildfire danger from Extreme to High. For the month of July, the Forestry Commission fought 430 fires, which consumed 8126 acres. A second heat wave occurred from the 17th through the 20th. During this time, numerous reporting stations rose above 100 degrees. A number of daily high temperatures records were broken, and additional daily records were broken for warmest low temperatures. The highest temperature recorded was 110 at Arkadelphia. Readings of 109 were observed at Russellville, Hot Springs airport, Cabot, and Morrilton. Stations reaching 108 included Little Rock, Mena, Dardanelle, Nimrod Dam, and Oden. Thereafter, temperatures moderated somewhat but still remained above normal. Another heat wave occurred from the 28th through the end of the month. During this period, the highest temperatures recorded were 112 at the Searcy airport, 111 at Little Rock, 110 at Cabot and Silver Hill, and 109 at Little Rock Air Force Base, the Batesville airport, Des Arc, and Evening Shade (forestry station).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A very well-developed dust devil damaged four chicken houses near Delaware. Tin was torn off the roof and sides of the chicken houses. The debris was pulled so high into the air that it flew over trees and ridges. Cattle and horses were frightened and ran.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The Fremont County emergency manager took several well defined photographs of a dust devil east of Newdale at around 1:15 pm MDT.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fremont County emergency manager took several well defined photographs of a dust devil east of Newdale at around 1:15 pm MDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil enchanted residents of central Maui as it spun west of Kula.  The phenomenon caused no serious property damage or injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Temperatures rose well into the 90s across much of western Montana which allowed a strong dust devil to form north of Rexford. A school was damaged as a result.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A member of the public in West Kootenai observed a strong and long-lived dust devil that caused roof damage to the Amish school and cut power momentarily at a warehouse. They said this was the strongest one they had ever experienced there in decades.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Warm, dry, and unstable conditions with a very weak layer of mid-level moisture produced a destructive dust devil over Los Alamos.  This dust devil produced damage to Barranca Elementary school.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Roof of gymnasium torn off and dropped onto library and playground area at Barranca Mesa Elementary School.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A formation of a dust devil caused damaged to a building in Redding, CA while California was under westerly flow aloft and winds were converging near the surface in the Northern Sacramento Valley. No injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An EF0 dust devil damaged the metal roof of a commercial building. The non-thunderstorm wind damage lasted a duration of approximately 5 minutes, at around 11:15-11:20 AM PDT on June, 19th. The damage included metal and wood roofing that was peeled backward, with some of the roofing landing on the adjacent ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong westerly flow ahead of a storm system brought downslope winds to the Owens Valley and isolated high winds to the southern Great Basin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil blew over two small travel trailers and damaged a solar panel.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, dry, and unstable airmass combined with a weak mid level moist layer produced a well defined and large dust devil or landspout tornado hybrid over the Estancia Valley.  Numerous pictures were obtained of this feature which garnered signature local media coverage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large dust devil or landspout tornado tore through open rangeland from near Estancia to Moriarty producing significant local media attention.  No damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot temperatures and light surface winds were conducive to dust devil development.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A nearly translucent, but powerful dust devil damaged the roof to one home on Tucson's east side.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot temperatures and light surface winds were conducive to dust devil development.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A powerful dust devil removed several dozen roof tiles from two homes in Green Valley. Wind speeds were estimated at 65 mph.  A stove vent was also blown off one roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dry Canadian high pressure, centered over western Ohio to start the day, made its way across the mid Atlantic, resulting in clear skies, very light northeasterly winds and afternoon temperatures roughly 5 to 8 degrees below normal for mid-September for much of the region.  The dust devil is thought to be the result of differential heating at the interface between different surface types.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil lifted several large, tied-down canopy tents into the air. The canopies then dropped down onto a crowd of people. There were six minor injuries, with one person taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm day combined with drought conditions led to the development of Dust Devils.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil moved from land to the Lake Monona shoreline and tipped over a Pontoon boat and the hoist that it was sitting on. Pier damage also occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level Pacific low pressure system brought strong, gusty and damaging winds to portions of southeast California on April 8th, especially the lower deserts of Imperial county. Gusty southwest to west winds developed during the morning hours, and continued into the early evening, prompting issuance of numerous products, including Wind Advisories, Blowing Dust Advisories, and High Wind Warnings. Peak gusts in excess of 60 mph were seen at times, strong enough to damage area trees and weaker structures such as sheds. The strong gradient winds were not associated with thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A powerful spring storm brought windy conditions to much of eastern Riverside county during the day on April 8th. Wind gusts in excess of 40 mph were common, and led to the issuance of a Wind Advisory which ran from 10 am PDT to 8 pm PDT. According to an on-line article posted on the KESQ.COM website, at 205 pm a dust devil struck the Salton City RV Resort in Salton City California. The dust devil combined with the already strong and gusty winds to produce damage at the RV park. Awnings were down, some siding was ripped off and a water pipe was broken. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil formed in the heat of a warm June day, causing damage to a home in Vail, AZ.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil blew shingles off a roof and an awning into a neighboring property, damaging the cover of a pickup truck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A possible Dust Devil was reportedly responsible for one fatality of a Sky Diver in Calverton. The instructor was injured as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Low level instability and convergence along a sea breeze front might have produced a dust devil that resulted in the death of 1 Sky Diver, and injured another.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very strong dust devil hit a shopping center on the edge of Prescott and caused damage to the building, merchandise, and customer vehicles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A very strong dust devil went through the Pioneer Village Shopping Center near the the intersection of Highway 89 and 69 in Prescott.  The strong winds blew out windows in a building, tossed free standing sheds (for sale) around, damaged cars, and threw shopping carts around.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm that developed over the Albuquerque International Sunport shifted slowly west into Albuquerque's South Valley late on the 15th.  This storm produced very heavy rainfall, strong winds, and a large dust devil or gustnado within the south valley corridor. Local broadcast media reported downed tree limbs and power lines with power outages for several hours. Residents indicated minor damage to landscaping with grills and other outdoor items tossed around.  However, no significant widespread flooding or major damage was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Large dust devil reported in south valley area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy southwest winds developed across south central Arizona during the afternoon hours on April 30th in association with an area of low pressure which developed across the desert southwest. In addition to the breezy conditions, the atmosphere was sunny, dry and unstable. The conditions were favorable for the formation of dust devils. A dust devil developed in Cave Creek during the early afternoon hours, and the associated strong winds damaged the roof of a local nursery. No injuries were reported due to the roof damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: During the early afternoon hours on April 30th, a strong dust devil developed approximately 3 miles south of Cave Creek. As reported by local broadcast media, KTVK Channel 3 TV,  gusty winds estimated to be in excess of 45 mph damaged the roof of the Desert Foothills Gardens Nursery. An aluminum roof panel on the top of the roof was lifted and tossed nearly 30 feet by the dust devil. The weight of the panel was estimated to be 600 pounds, and the dimensions were approximately 55 by 35 feet. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gusty northerly and easterly winds increased over the Central Valley, Delta, Southern Lake County, and Sierra Nevada and foothills. The event began early Tuesday March 11 and continued for some areas as late as mid-day Wednesday.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil developed on the property near an old tin roofed barn. As the dust devil encountered the barn, a large section of the tin roof was ripped off and the pieces were thrown several hundred feet into the air. A neighbor reported that one of the pieces was found almost a mile down the road. The individual tin sections were about 6 feet long and 2 feet wide. Approximately 35-40 tin panels were ripped off the barn. The dust devil lasted for around 2 minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm began impacting Utah on March 25, bringing increasing winds, followed by showers on March 26. Most of these winds, rain showers, and snow showers did not have any significant impacts, but two isolated events in southern Utah reached severe levels.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trampoline was blown out of a backyard and into some power lines in Minersville. Recorded wind gusts in the area at the time were relatively light, so it is likely that this was caused by a strong dust devil. Time listed is approximate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil occurred in Manahawkin (Ocean County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dust devil tossed a trampoline over a fence in Manahawkin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dust devil touched down producing roof damage at a local greenhouse. Overall conditions in the area were benign with mostly cloudy skies, temperatures in the mid 50s and NNW winds at around 10 to 15 mph throughout the afternoon hours. A weak non-meteorological echo was caught on radar in the area of damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Roof damage with broken panels was reported to 3 greenhouses with swirling wind/dirt reported in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure over the Great Basin brought very strong and gusty northeast to east winds and hot weather from the 12th through the 14th, before the winds finally decreased. The hardest hit areas were the mountains and western foothills of Riverside and San Diego County. The gusty winds downed countless trees, power lines and blew tiles from roofs. The winds also helped to fuel and spread nearly a dozen wildfires in San Diego County alone. The hot weather even spawned a damaging dust devil early on, before the winds really got going.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public reported a dust devil near Fullerton that came abruptly out of the west carrying large amounts of dust and leaves, and damaged portions of roof shingles on a few homes with estimated wind gusts of 60 mph.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the morning of the seventh, a mesoscale convective system moving across Oklahoma reinforced pre-existing outflow boundaries in the Rolling Plains and eastern South Plains. A weak short wave moving over the top of an upper level ridge combined with a very unstable airmass over the Rolling Plains creating scattered severe thunderstorms. Strong downdraft CAPE values led to very strong reported wind gusts as well as large hail to the size of golf balls. Strong winds blew over a tractor trailer near Kirkland (Childress County) along US Highway 287. In addition, repeated rounds of slow moving thunderstorms dropped several inches of rain on far southwestern Childress County. An NWS cooperative weather observer reported 4.48 inches of rainfall while radar rainfall estimates were between five and six inches just a few miles east of the observer's location.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Muleshoe recorded a wind gust to 63 mph. However, an NWS cooperative weather observer viewed a dust devil moving across the mesonet location at the same time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A significant dust devil formed in the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the afternoon hours on May 4th. The dust devil formed about 7 miles southwest of central Phoenix during the middle of the afternoon and managed to damage the tile roofs of about 6 homes. EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong dust devil developed in the central portion of the greater Phoenix area during the middle of the afternoon on May 4. The dust devil was reported by a member of the public; at 1505MST the dust devil managed to produce roof tile damage to 6 houses in Laveen Village, just west of South Mountain Park and about 7 miles to the southwest of central Phoenix. This was a significant dust devil; pictures of the devil were obtained and posted on social media. No injuries were reported due to the dust devil.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Prior to cloud and thunderstorm development that afternoon, a dust devil formed during the morning hours, causing damage and one injury in Sierra Vista.
